title: Can't SSH into production EC2 instances
description: I SSH into the EC2 instances behind the production load balancer via the bastion, and they all time out.

worklogs.description: Checked Security Group inbound rules, port 22 is only open for the bastion — no changes.
Reviewed the bastion host /var/log/auth.log — the connection reaches the bastion but the EC2 rejects it.
Searched CloudTrail for a KeyRotation event in the last 24 hours — none found.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: The bastion is reachable but the backend EC2s are rejecting the connection. I need to check a few things: (1) which pem file are you using, and what's its filename/fingerprint? Command: ssh-keygen -lf <key.pem>. (2) Could you share the '-v' output of your last SSH command? Something like 'ssh -v -i key.pem ec2-user@10.0.5.x'.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: I'm using prod-eu-2024.pem. ssh-keygen output: SHA256:abc123def456... I've attached the verbose output.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: I reviewed the verbose output — the server is throwing 'Permission denied (publickey)'. This indicates your pem file isn't in that instance's authorized_keys list. Do you know if we did a key rotation in the past week? If so, you were probably issued a new pem file.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: I couldn't find the event in CloudTrail, but maybe it was done via manual SSH. I've asked the user's team lead, waiting for a reply.
